pro_course_detail.title: 👄 Accent Reduction with American English Accent Modeling (*Neutral American English)
pro_course_detail.description:
(This is not a conversation class, though some converation will be used in diagnostics and practice modeling. This is an Accent Reduction and pronunciation correction class, with the goal of approaching a Neutral American Accent (also called the 'Midwestern Accent'). The first sessions are dedicated to an extensive phonemic diagnostic based on students' existing natural speech, minimal pair tests, sample texts and other assessments. 

** IMPORTANT:  Please let me know before our first session what your native language is, i.e., the language you grew up speaking, even if it's not your current dominant language **

All students booking sessions with me get to benefit from my 30+ year background in broadcast and voiceover training, and my neutral Midwest [Ohio, USA] accent.

Special attention is placed on diagnosing and remedying phonetic distortion and inaccuracies which may stem from the learner's native language pronunciation and intonation patterns, previous poor training, and so forth.  All learners in my Accent Reduction sessions have different needs, depending on particular pronunciation issues, so the first session is spent diagnosing pronunciation issues, with exercises provided for home-study and practice. 

Accent reduction sessions are focused and intense, so I would suggest booking a 30 or 45 minute accent reduction/pronunciation session, followed by a more 'relaxing' one hour General Conversation or Public Speaking Session as an ideal combo.

pro_course_detail.description:
We'll discuss fun topics together, and you get to choose! The structure is similar to conversation practice for test preparation, but more relaxed.

Topics:
City/town - We will chat about life in towns and cities, including our own! In my case I have lived in Miami and all over Spain.

Movies/series - We will talk about the movies and series we love (or hate)! 

Music - We will discuss our favorite genres and our own experiences! Everything from concerts and festivals, to our own performances and how music is viewed in our cultures.

Books and short stories - What makes a good story? Our favorite stories and what they mean to us.

Art - What is art? We may converse about different types of art, the art we create, art in our lives, and philosophic questions such as: what is beauty? Is art subjective or objective? What is the purpose of art in a society?

Philosophy - Subjects ranging from free will, the mind, different philosophers, metaphysics, ethics, or anything else the student is interested in.

Science - We can talk about different scientific discoveries, advancements and what we can expect in the future, life on other planets.

Sleep/dreams - Everything from our sleeping patterns to lucid dreaming (controlling our own dreams, something I can do, and maybe I can teach you how to do it too!)

Food - The foods in our countries, foods we love and hate, rstaurants, cooking, different diets (like vegetarian or vegan), and all things food!

Anecdotes - These can be anything that's happened to us or someone we know. Could be anything  ranging from fun adventures, scary moments, broken bones, times we got in trouble, or just anything you would like to share. 

Goals - Our plans for the future, dream jobs, and where we want to end up. A great way to practice the future tense!

Student's suggestion! - We can talk about anything you'd like! Make a suggestions and we can discuss it.

Combination - Combine any of the topics above for a fun and dynamic conversation class!

Many students tell me they really appreciate my bright personality and eagerness to listening. I would have to agree with them.The amount of time I spend talking is directly related to the level of the student. I like to follow the 40/60 rule for beginners, the 70/30 rule for intermediate learners and the 90/10 rule for advanced students. 

This means that if you are just starting to learn a language, you should be speaking 40% of the lesson, 70% if you are at an intermediate level, and 90% if you are at an advanced level. If you ever feel like your teacher is talking too much during the class, you're probably right! Feel free to let us know. I personally enjoy when students push boundaries.
teacher_info.teaching_style:
I offer two types of lessons: conversational and traditional. 

My traditional classes are guided by grammar.
My conversation lessons are my most popular. You can expect to have a specific topic, for example "the importance of work ethic" where I will ask you specific questions. In these lessons, I will focus on making corrections as you speak while also asking you follow up questions related to grammar. For example if you say "I didn't do nothing" I will give you a chance to correct yourself -->(I didn't do ANYTHING).After we discover the correct answer, I would ask you "What is the difference between anything vs nothing? This way we are practicing conversation but at the same time grammar.
